what: The golden sets can now be run in this environment, which is what gates every retrieval, prompt, chunking and grounding change. Running them immediately found a defect in the gate itself: it reported a determinism figure it had not measured.
why_it_matters: Roughly half the remaining roadmap is retrieval or prompt work, and the project's own rule is that none of it merges without both golden sets. Without a model here, that rule made those changes unshippable rather than ungated - so the work kept being deferred in favour of things that needed no gate.

how.models: The two files the desktop app ships with, fetched by the project's OWN downloader (openknowledge.desktop.download.ensure_model) so that path was exercised too: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M (2.5 GB) and nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M (84 MB), each verified against the SHA-256 pinned in desktop/manifest.py.
how.runtime: llama-cpp-python's OpenAI-compatible server, two processes - chat on 8081 with an 8192-token window, embeddings on 8082 - matching the windows the manifest records. GitHub is unreachable from this container for anything outside the scoped repository (403 on codeload and on release assets), so a prebuilt llama.cpp binary was not an option; PyPI is reachable directly and ships the source.
how.profile: The `self-hosted` profile from evals/profiles.yaml: local tier only, no ladder, no escalation, so the numbers are this model's own and nothing is billed.

measured.speed: 71.6s for a realistic case - 1,917-token prompt, 99-token completion - on 4 CPUs. About 1.4 tokens/sec generating. That puts the 13-case golden set in minutes and the 26-case aveline set in roughly half an hour, single-pass. Gating a change costs an hour of wall-clock, not seconds, which is worth knowing before promising fast iteration.
measured.golden_set: 13 cases: accuracy 100% over 8 answerable, 0 false answers across 5 must-refuse, paraphrase consistency 100%, $0.00. The free retrieval pre-flight passed first, so a live failure would have been the model's and not the corpus's.
measured.caveat: This is a 4B model where the profile's own default is qwen3:8b. A weak number here would measure the model, not the retrieval, and must be read that way.

the_defect_it_found.what: `--no-determinism` asks each question once. The report said 'determinism 100.0% (same question twice)' anyway, because the per-case flag defaulted to True and nothing distinguished 'checked and identical' from 'never asked'.
the_defect_it_found.why_it_is_worse_than_a_wrong_label: --save-baseline wrote that 1.0 into the saved baseline. A later run that genuinely asked twice and scored 90% would have been reported as a regression against a figure nobody had ever measured. The first baseline written in this environment contained exactly that: determinism 1.0, from a run that never asked anything twice.
the_defect_it_found.fixed: The per-case flag is None when unchecked; the report says 'not checked' rather than a percentage; the baseline records null; and the comparison runs only when both runs actually measured. Skipping does not fail a run - the caller asked for it - but it no longer passes one either, because there is nothing to pass.
the_defect_it_found.found_how: By reading the output of the first real run rather than accepting that it said PASSED. The number was 100% for a check the command line had explicitly turned off.

every_test_was_checked_against_the_bug_i: Five sabotages, each applied and run: default the per-case flag back to True, call an unmeasured determinism 100%, write the unmeasured figure into the baseline, compare against a baseline that never measured, and compare when this run never measured. One passed the first time - every test built its CaseResult by hand and passed the flag itself, so nothing exercised run_case's own default. A test that goes through the real runner with the check turned off now covers it, and all five fail against their bug.
what_this_unblocks: Retrieval and prompt changes can now be gated by running both sets and comparing against a saved baseline that fails on regressions, instead of by judgement: the cross-encoder reranker, contextual chunk embedding, folder scoping, and the must_not_say harness gap.
still_open: The escalation rate, draft yield and gate pass rate on a paid tier are still assumed - this measures a self-hosted rung, which is one of the four configurations tools/compare_configs.py exists to compare. That still needs an API key.
